artifact.name: knix.img
artifact.role: GPT disk with a 512 MiB FAT32 EFI system partition and an ext4 root; native rootfs, self-built 7.2.15 kernel, 773 modules (including virtio-gpu and virtio-input), guest-owned initramfs, systemd-boot, a guest-owned DRM device, a guest-owned seatd session unit that runs sway as knix and a guest-owned systemd OnFailure= crash diagnostic

seed.name: debian-13-generic-arm64.qcow2
seed.role: one-time package source and helper boot; not a product capability source

build_baseline.rule: build.sh --build refuses to assemble when any guest-produced summary or the package lockfile differs from these locked values

build_stages: platform/image/build-kernel.sh --apply (inside the arm64 Linux build guest)
platform/image/build-rootfs.sh --apply (inside the arm64 Linux build guest; also writes package-versions.txt)
platform/image/build.sh --build (on the host; verifies the locked baseline, assembles, UEFI cold-boots, verifies identity/brand/graphics/framebuffer, writes the receipt)
verification: uname -m is aarch64 and uname -r is 7.2.15
/boot/vmlinuz-7.2.15-knix is byte-identical to kernel-build.json
/etc/os-release reports NAME=Knix ID=knix VERSION=0.1 (bootstrap)
hostname is knix
/lib/modules/7.2.15 carries the recorded module count and modules.dep
modprobe loads a module without vermagic or unknown-symbol errors
4 brand assets are byte-identical to docs/brand/
no cloud-init state, no seed bootloader, no failed units
boots from its own EFI system partition with no -kernel, no seed ISO and no EFI boot variables
/efi/EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI, /efi/loader/entries/knix.conf, vmlinuz and initrd are present
cfg80211 loads the upstream-signed regulatory.db without a rejection in dmesg
/dev/dri/card0 and renderD128 are guest-owned DRM nodes bound to virtio_gpu
card0-Virtual-1 exposes a 1280x800 mode and guest virtio keyboard/pointer nodes exist
knix-session.service is enabled by multi-user.target and already active as knix before any verification script runs, from WLR_BACKENDS=drm,libinput through the guest's seatd
swaymsg -t get_inputs reports the virtio keyboard and tablet; the guest udev rule tags both nodes seat+uaccess and knix holds video/input/render
swaymsg reports Virtual-1 active on the DRM backend
the sway log shows an allocated GBM buffer and a created GL FBO
foot connects as a Wayland client, appears in get_tree and commits wlr_surfaces
after SIGKILL the guest's own systemd restarts sway as knix and the restarted session again provides DRM, libinput, GBM/GL and a Wayland client window
the restarted sway paints a guest-chosen 24-bit colour on the standard virtio-gpu scanout
QMP screendump (P6) of that scanout shows the guest colour at 9/9 sample points plus guest swaybar pixels before any receipt is written
sshd -T refuses root, password, keyboard-interactive and empty passwords and requires public keys; a real password login attempt and a root login attempt are both rejected by the guest sshd
knix is the only interactive account, root and knix passwords are locked, no root login session exists and loginctl reports knix active on a graphical seat0
the guest logind carries an explicit IdleAction=ignore policy, no getty autologin override exists and the kiosk session is started by multi-user.target before any verification script touches it
a deliberate crash loop makes guest systemd refuse further restarts, leaving ActiveState=failed, zero sway processes, exactly one failed unit (the session unit) and ssh plus the serial console intact
after the crash loop the guest's own systemd recovers a knix-owned sway with DRM, libinput, GBM/GL and a Wayland client, which then paints the verified framebuffer pattern
the guest's own systemd OnFailure= unit writes /run/knix/session-failure.txt from guest unit state, journal and local device nodes, with no host input
verify-graphics.sh requires the guest report to describe the final failed state and the guest history to contain more than one reported crash before any receipt is written

the guest OnFailure= script keeps cross-boot statistics, a bounded rotated archive and an err-priority journal alert with a login-visible notice; verify-graphics.sh requires DIAGNOSTICS OPS VERIFY OK and ROTATION VERIFY OK from an isolated /run drill

build.sh relaunches the same disk and requires DIAGNOSTICS OPS PERSISTENCE VERIFY OK: a guest-triggered failure in the second boot must add a new boot id to the archive and advance the statistics before any receipt is written

the same guest OnFailure= script recomputes a bounded per-boot trend report from its own archive family: events, failed states, start-limit hits, restart peak and first/last timestamps per boot, plus cumulative boots_seen / total_events / limit_boots / max_events_per_boot
verify-graphics.sh requires TRENDS VERIFY OK: the trend report matches the guest statistics, its rows sum exactly, stays within 8 boots / 4096 bytes and never rewrites the production archive
build.sh requires DIAGNOSTICS TRENDS PERSISTENCE VERIFY OK: after the guest reports a failure in the second boot the trend report must carry both boots before any receipt is written
GPU=none leaves the autostart condition unmet and keeps the serial console and ssh as the full fallback path, with zero failed units
build.sh compares every kernel/rootfs summary field and both lockfiles against build_baseline before assembling
scripts/verify-repro.py checks all pinned inputs, the lockfile and the absence of binary build artifacts

boot.esp: 512 MiB FAT32 on /dev/vda1; removable path EFI/BOOT/BOOTAA64.EFI

authentication.rule: the guest owns every account, credential and login decision; sshd accepts public keys only for knix, root and every password path are refused, the kiosk session is started by the guest's own target without a getty autologin override, and logind keeps an explicit no-auto-suspend idle policy
authentication.verification: build.sh --build runs verify-login.sh before the graphics gate and refuses a receipt unless LOGIN POLICY OK and LOGIN VERIFY OK are both present
authentication.fallback: GPU=none keeps the serial console and key-based ssh; no password, root or host-supplied login is ever enabled

graphics.fallback: GPU=none leaves the session unit's /dev/dri/card0 condition unmet; the serial console and ssh remain the full fallback path

framebuffer.capture: QMP screendump (P6) of the standard virtio-gpu scanout
framebuffer.pattern: guest-chosen 24-bit colour from /dev/urandom, painted by the restarted sway as a solid-colour background
framebuffer.rule: build.sh --build captures the headless framebuffer after the guest paints and refuses to write a receipt unless all 9 sampled pixels equal the guest-reported colour and the guest swaybar is visible
framebuffer.fallback: GPU=none leaves the scanout unowned; the serial console and ssh remain the full fallback path

resilience.verification: SIGKILL the compositor and require guest systemd to restore a knix-owned sway with DRM, libinput and a Wayland client

crash_loop.verification: build.sh --build requires LIMIT VERIFY OK before the guest paints the framebuffer pattern: repeated SIGKILL must make guest systemd stop restarting, leave exactly one failed unit with ssh and the serial console intact, and then recover a complete knix-owned session
crash_loop.fallback: serial console and ssh stay available while the compositor unit is failed; a crash loop never becomes a host-managed capability

diagnostics.trigger: OnFailure=knix-session-failure.service on knix-session.service; systemd invokes the oneshot once per failed state
diagnostics.format: key=value lines in the report, one line per reported failure in the history
diagnostics.rule: verify-graphics.sh requires DIAGNOSTICS VERIFY OK: the guest-written report must describe the final failed state (active_state=failed, result=signal, exec_main_status=9, failed_units=1, zero sway processes, ssh and serial intact) and the history must record more than one crash

persistence.rule: assemble-native.sh pins Storage=persistent and the guest OnFailure= script appends every report to a boot-stamped archive on the root filesystem; the host never writes or collects diagnostics
persistence.verification: build.sh --build relaunches the same disk after the cold-boot verification and requires DIAGNOSTICS PERSISTENCE VERIFY OK: the archive still holds the terminal failed state, /run/knix is gone, the stored boot id is from the previous boot and journalctl still lists that boot
persistence.fallback: GPU=none produces no failed state, so no archive entry is written; the serial console and ssh remain the full fallback path

operations.rule: the guest OnFailure= script bounds and rotates its own archive, recomputes cross-boot statistics and raises a local err-priority journal alert with a login-visible notice; the host never writes, rotates or forwards diagnostics
operations.verification: verify-graphics.sh requires DIAGNOSTICS OPS VERIFY OK and ROTATION VERIFY OK from an isolated /run drill; build.sh --build relaunches the same disk, makes the guest report one failure in that second boot and requires DIAGNOSTICS OPS PERSISTENCE VERIFY OK before writing the receipt
operations.fallback: GPU=none produces no failed state, so no alert is raised; the serial console and ssh remain the full fallback path

trends.source: the same guest-owned session-failure.log archive family that produces the statistics
trends.rule: the same guest OnFailure= script recomputes a bounded per-boot profile from its own archive on every failure; no host collector, network service or external analytics channel is involved
trends.verification: verify-graphics.sh requires TRENDS VERIFY OK: guest-owned report, boots_seen and total_events equal the guest statistics, per-boot rows sum to trend_events_sum, all six fields present, rows within boot_limit and bytes within byte_limit, with the production archive and statistics byte-identical; build.sh --build relaunches the same disk and requires DIAGNOSTICS TRENDS PERSISTENCE VERIFY OK after a guest-triggered failure in the second boot
trends.fallback: GPU=none produces no failed state, so no trend row is added; the serial console and ssh remain the full fallback path

diagnostics.fallback: the guest-owned archive, statistics, trends, alert and persistent journal keep the durable record; /run/knix is only a runtime snapshot; GPU=none produces no failure and keeps the serial console and ssh as the full fallback path

baseline_refresh.ci_gate: --self-test exercises the policy without guest artifacts

receipt: platform/image/build.sh writes $KNIX_DEV_DIR/BUILD-RECEIPT.json (schema 3) with the artifact sha256, the canonical build_baseline sha256, the graphics.session verification result including autostart, crash recovery, crash-loop limiting, the number of guest-reported failure diagnostics, the guest-owned persistence and cross-boot operations proof, the graphics.framebuffer pixel proof, the guest-owned per-boot diagnostics trend report, and every build input digest

release.not_a_build_input: the release gate never enters inputs.*_sha256, so it does not change the receipt it judges
release.ci_gate: --self-test refuses tampered receipts and images in a temporary directory without a VM or a build artifact
